headline: Agentic AI Harnesses Evolve: Chains, Graphs, and Now Code
summary: InfoQ traces how agentic AI architectures have evolved from simple prompt chains to graph-based orchestration and now toward code-centric harnesses, where agents write and execute code to accomplish tasks rather than relying purely on structured prompt flows. The piece examines the tradeoffs in flexibility, reliability, and debuggability across these generations of agent design.
why_it_matters: As an AI Engineer building LLM applications on ServiceNow, understanding this architectural progression directly informs how you design and harden your own agentic workflows. Code-based harnesses in particular offer a pattern you could adopt to make agents more robust and auditable, which is central to your goal of becoming an AI Application Engineer.

headline: OpenAI Unveils GPT-6.1 Terra
summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Terra, a new model release positioned as an incremental but significant upgrade in capability, reasoning, and efficiency over prior GPT iterations.
why_it_matters: New frontier models like Terra shift the baseline for what's feasible in LLM application development. Staying current on model capabilities helps you evaluate whether and how to integrate newer models into ServiceNow/LLM workflows, keeping your engineering skills and tooling choices aligned with the state of the art.

headline: Free Video Course: Building Reasoning Models from Scratch
summary: Sebastian Raschka has released a from-scratch video course walking through how to build reasoning models, covering the underlying techniques and design choices that enable step-by-step reasoning in LLMs.
why_it_matters: This is a hands-on learning resource that can deepen your technical foundation in building and fine-tuning reasoning-capable models—valuable skill-building as you work toward the AI Application Engineer role, especially for designing more capable agentic systems.

headline: Tsinghua Open-Sources AKV, a KV-Cache Server for LLM Agents
summary: Researchers from Tsinghua have open-sourced AKV, a cache engineering server built for SGLang that optimizes key-value (KV) cache management for LLM agents, aiming to improve memory efficiency and throughput in agentic inference workloads.
why_it_matters: Efficient KV-cache handling is a practical infrastructure concern for anyone deploying LLM agents at scale. This open-source tool could be relevant if you're optimizing inference performance or cost for agent-based applications in your current ServiceNow/LLM work.

headline: AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026: Agentic AI Foundation Expands as MCP Focuses on Security
summary: The Agentic AI Foundation added four new projects at AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026, with a notable shift in focus toward security within the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem, reflecting growing maturity and governance concerns in agentic AI tooling.
why_it_matters: MCP is becoming a key standard for connecting agents to tools and data sources. The move toward security hardening is directly relevant to building production-grade LLM agent applications, and tracking which projects join the foundation can help you choose well-supported tools for your own engineering work.
